first.rationale: The objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so triage targets the two beliefs that are most decision-consequential and least supported for that specific objective. (1) memory_73 (promotional pricing) is the highest-pull option given the competitor's entry pricing, and it is exactly the belief whose recorded evidence — 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' — is stated in short-horizon acquisition terms with no retention or margin horizon. If its source record turns out to be a short-window acquisition test, discount-matching would likely buy churn-prone, low-quality volume and actively damage the objective; verifying it is the cheapest way to avoid a costly wrong turn. (2) memory_86 underwrites my intended action and speaks directly to the observed 4% onboarding-completion decline, but its recorded outcome is 'completion rates, time-to-value, early adoption' — proxy metrics, not qualified revenue. I need to know whether that lift ever propagated to paid conversion and retention, or stopped at the funnel. I did not spend budget on memory_31 because it is largely redundant with memory_86 (same mechanism, self-serve/SMB activation) and on memory_44/memory_57 because enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives address neither of the two metrics that are actually degrading this quarter. Current intent: simplify_onboarding as a standard experiment. It is the only direction that addresses both declining metrics at their shared root (activation is downstream of onboarding completion), it is supported by two independently consolidated memories rather than one, and it competes with the discounting competitor on delivered value rather than on price, which is the version of the response that compounds instead of eroding. Two caveats I am holding open rather than resolving by assumption: the inherited evidence is adoption-level, not revenue-level, so a completion lift may not convert into qualified revenue; and field removal at signup can strip the firmographic data used for lead qualification and routing, meaning a 'successful' test could raise volume while lowering qualified pipeline. I will therefore instrument on qualified-pipeline and 30/60-day retention, not completion rate alone, and treat lead-quality degradation as a stopping condition. If the memory_73 archive shows a genuine long-horizon retention-clean result, I will revisit pricing next cycle; if the memory_86 archive shows the lift never reached revenue, I will fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the activation decline with a lighter footprint and no qualification-data risk.

final.rationale: Both pulls paid off, and in opposite directions. exp_73 is now explicitly disqualified for this objective: +31% signup and +18% qualified revenue came with -12% 30-day retention, and the original record's own conclusion warns against generalizing targeted discounting as sustainable growth. That is precisely the failure mode I flagged — short-horizon acquisition gains masking a cohort that does not survive first renewal. Matching the competitor's entry pricing is therefore off the table this week despite being the most reflexively urgent response; memory_73 is retired as support for any sustainable-revenue action and should be re-consolidated with that caveat attached. exp_86 came back confirmed and, importantly, stronger than the inherited summary: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. The retention figure is what matters — it converts my main worry (that the lift stopped at funnel proxies) into evidence that the gain propagates past the first renewal window rather than borrowing from it. Combined with memory_31 (independent, same mechanism, durable first-week activation lift) and the fact that activation is downstream of onboarding completion, this single intervention addresses both degrading metrics at a shared root and competes on delivered value rather than price. Final decision: simplify_onboarding at standard experiment scale. Not broad rollout — exp_86 still measures retention at 30 days, not qualified revenue over a full renewal cycle, so the revenue link remains inferred rather than demonstrated, and one confirmed record plus one corroborating memory does not license skipping the measurement step. Residual risk I am carrying, not dismissing: removing signup fields can strip the firmographic data used for lead qualification and routing, so raw volume could rise while qualified pipeline falls. Instrumentation will therefore be qualified pipeline and 30/60-day retention as primary, with completion rate demoted to a diagnostic, and lead-quality degradation set as an explicit stopping condition. If qualified pipeline moves against completion, I stop and fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91), which targets the activation decline without touching qualification data. The competitor pricing pressure is real but is now a known trap; the durable answer to a discounter is time-to-value, which is what this test buys.
